drivingQuestion: Why would a get dated by the wrong kingdom carry the full penalties?
outcomeNote: The severity is explained as R' Meir's view on any deviation from the Sages' formula.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ מַאי ״מַלְכוּת שֶׁאֵינָהּ הוֹגֶנֶת״? רוֹמִי. וְאַמַּאי קָרֵי לַהּ מַלְכוּת שֶׁאֵינָהּ הוֹגֶנֶת? מִשּׁוּם דְּאֵין לָהֶם לֹא כְּתָב, וְלֹא לָשׁוֹן.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» It was stated in the mishna that if one wrote the date on a bill of divorce according to a kingdom that is not legitimate, it is invalid. The Gemara asks: «What» is the meaning of the description: «A kingdom that is not legitimate?» The Gemara answers: This is referring to «the Roman Empire,» and he wrote the bill of divorce in a different country, such as Babylonia, where the Romans were not in power. «And why is it called: A kingdom that is not legitimate? Because they have neither» their own «script, nor» their own «language,» but rather, they took them from other nations.

segments.he: אָמַר עוּלָּא: מִפְּנֵי מָה תִּיקְּנוּ מַלְכוּת בְּגִיטִּין – מִשּׁוּם שְׁלוֹם מַלְכוּת.
segments.en: «Ulla said: For what» reason «did» the Sages «institute» that the date should be written according to the years of the local «kingdom, in bills of divorce? Due to» the need to maintain «peaceful» relations with «the kingdom,» as the government is particular that important documents issued in its domain be written with the date of that government.

segments.he: וּמִשּׁוּם שְׁלוֹם מַלְכוּת – תֵּצֵא וְהַוָּלָד מַמְזֵר?!
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «But due to» an ordinance instituted by the Sages solely for the sake of maintaining «peaceful» relations with «the kingdom,» would they be so stringent that the woman would be forced to «leave» her husband, «and» they would declare the status of «the offspring is a mamzer?»

segments.he: אִין, רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְטַעְמֵיהּ – דְּאָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא, אוֹמֵר הָיָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר: כָּל הַמְשַׁנֶּה מִמַּטְבֵּעַ שֶׁטָּבְעוּ חֲכָמִים בְּגִיטִּין – הַוָּלָד מַמְזֵר.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «Yes. Rabbi Meir» conforms «to his» line of «reasoning. As Rav Hamnuna says in the name of Ulla: Rabbi Meir would say» that «anyone deviating from the formula coined by the Sages for bills of divorce,» even if it is only a minor deviation, the bill of divorce is invalid, and if the woman remarried on the basis of this bill of divorce, then «the offspring» from that marriage «is a mamzer.»
